     * `num_stages=1`

     * forcing fla's `ASCEND_UB_CAPACITY_BITS` env var down to its 512-KiB fallback (fla-side tiling then still legitimately picks BK/BV=64 for K=V=64)

So the extra 2048 bits appear to be structural in the plan-memory/UB-budgeting for this kernel shape, not an optional-feature buffer.

@ChenxiQ

Thanks for the follow-up — you're right: this is a regression on our side. We have since bisected it to a single compiler commit. Your three questions:

1. Is it already known / fixed in a newer daily? It is not fixed in any newer build — we re-ran the same repro on the newest build we have and it still fails with the identical `1574912/1572864`.

Root cause: `bishengir` commit `931106de0` (2026-08-04), titled `[AscendNPU IR][NFC] Fix style issues`. It corrects a guard in `WorklistBuilder` that was miscounting `annotation.mark` users. With the guard fixed, CV pipelining fires for this kernel for the first time and expands the loop-carried workspace by the pipeline depth (`--set-workspace-multibuffer`, default 4 on A3):
    
    `memref<64x64xf32>  ──expandWorkspace──▶  memref<4x64x64xf32>   (64 KiB each)
    `

Two such buffers live for the whole kernel → 128 KiB of UB pinned → the plan lands at 196864 B vs the 196608 B budget (256 B over). Before that commit the pass silently exited without doing anything on this loop (the guard misjudged and returned early — no error, no build failure), so pipelining was effectively disabled for kernels like this. The depth is only a multiplier: with the pass doing nothing, the `4` had nothing to multiply, hence harmless.

Note: the above is our preliminary analysis from bisecting the compiler. Please file the issue in the `bishengir` repo, which owns the fix, to have it confirmed there.

2. Will the fix make it into 3.6.0? The currently released 3.6.0 does not contain a fix. The defect is in `bishengir`, not triton-ascend — so the fix will be included in a bishengir daily build or release published after the bishengir team fixes it.

3. Where to file it? Yes, please — two issues, since the defect and the symptom live in different repos:

     * `Ascend/AscendNPU-IR` — the compiler; this is where the fix has to land:
https://gitcode.com/Ascend/AscendNPU-IR/issues
     * this repo (`triton-lang/triton-ascend`) — tracking the user-visible symptom, and please paste the `AscendNPU-IR` issue link into it so the two are cross-linked.

Suggested scope for the compiler one: "chunk_kda bwd `wy_dw_part` no longer fits the 192-KiB UB: bishengir regression introduced by `931106de0` (2026-08-04; the 08-03 sync passes, the 08-06 sync fails)". --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#### CANN

Prior to starting work with SGLang on Ascend, you need to install CANN Toolkit, Kernels operator package and NNAL version 9.1.0, check the installation guide

#### MemFabric-Hybrid

If you want to use PD disaggregation mode, you need to install MemFabric-Hybrid. MemFabric-Hybrid is a drop-in replacement of Mooncake Transfer Engine that enables KV cache transfer on Ascend NPU clusters.
    
    # On an x86_64 host, use memfabric_hybrid-1.2.1-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_27_x86_64.manylinux_2_28_x86_64.whl from the same directory instead
    pip install https://obs-memfabric-hybrid.obs.cn-north-4.myhuaweicloud.com/mf/v1.2.1/20260923.4/memfabric_hybrid-1.2.1-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_26_aarch64.manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl
    
    # Install the device-specific MemFabric kernels:
    # --soc-version is A5 on the 950PR/DT Series, A3 on the A3 Series
    
    python3 -c "import torch; print(torch.npu.is_available()); x = torch.arange(1, 5, dtype=torch.float32).npu(); print(x * x)"

The expected second line is `tensor([1., 4., 9., 16.], device='npu:0')` — the squares of `1, 2, 3, 4`, computed on the device. You may also see some compatibility warnings caused by device differences; they are safe to ignore.

#### Triton on Ascend

We provide our own implementation of Triton for Ascend.
    
    # On an x86_64 host, replace aarch64 with x86_64 in the wheel URL
    pip install https://github.com/triton-lang/triton-ascend/releases/download/v3.2.2/triton_ascend-3.2.2-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_27_aarch64.manylinux_2_28_aarch64.whl

For installation of Triton on Ascend nightly builds or from sources, follow installation guide

#### SGLang Kernels NPU

We provide SGL kernels for Ascend NPU, check installation guide.

Gemma-family models (including Qwen3.5) call `sgl_kernel_npu.norm.gemma_rmsnorm`, whose implementation is chosen when the wheel is built: the native `torch_npu` operator for A2/A3 series, and ACLNN RMSNorm for 950PR/DT series, which does not register that operator. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[Bug] MRV2: Engram lookback Triton kernel dereferences masked lanes with negative offsets when batch == max_num_seqs (devmm 534 → 507035) on Ascend 910B#21392

triaged

opened on Nov 10, 2026

### Summary

With MRV2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`) on Ascend 910B3, the Engram lookback Triton kernel
(`vllm_ascend/ops/triton/engram_lookback.py:10`, `_gather_lookback_kernel`; called from
`vllm_ascend/models/deepseek_v41/engram/model_state.py:117`) dereferences out-of-range addresses for
masked lanes. As soon as the batch reaches `max_num_seqs`, the first real forward triggers:
    
    `[devmm] devmm_dev_page_fault_get_vaflgs 534: Va error don't allow fault by device
            (va=0x12d2ffe00000, 8 TP ranks, same VA)
    engine: 507035 vector core execution is abnormal -> rtDeviceSynchronizeWithTimeout -> EngineCore killed
request: the warmup path uses `_dummy_run(skip_attn=True)` and never launches this kernel.

### Evidence

(a) Exception dump (`NPU_COLLECT_PATH=/… ASCEND_WORK_PATH=/…`) prints the kernel name and its args:
    
    `GetBinAndKernelNameExceptionArgs: kernel_name=_gather_lookback_kernel
    GetArgsInfo: args(0..10) = … 0x12d300000000, 0x1000020000, 0x100000010 …, blockDim=16
    `

`0x12d300000000` is `all_token_ids.data_ptr()`; the low 32 bits of `0x1000020000` are 131072 =
`all_token_ids.stride(0)`; the low 32 bits of `0x100000010` are 16 = `num_reqs` (= `blockDim`, full batch).
The faulting VA reported by devmm is `data_ptr - 2 MB` (the tensor is 2 MB-aligned, so any access at
`ptr - k, 0 < k < 2 MB` is reported at that same page).

(b) Per-launch tracing (a `sitecustomize.py` hook on `triton.runtime.jit.JITFunction.run`,
`ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`) captures the args of every launch. The crashing launch is:
    
    `#3  nreq=8  idx_mapping=[7,6,4,3,0,5,2,1]  num_computed=[0,0,0,0,0,0,17,21]  stride=131072  window=(8,3)
buffer (unmapped) -> devmm 534; for `req_state_idx > 0` the negative offset still lands inside the
buffer (tail of the previous row), so only the `req_state_idx == 0` row faults.

The same kernel, line-identical in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/model_state.py:17`, does not crash
on GPU — which points at backend address predication rather than kernel logic.

Secondary robustness issue: the load in (A) has no mask, so a negative/garbage `req_state_idx` would
read out of range as well.


### Suggested fix
    
    pos = num_computed - 1 - offs
    valid = in_batch & (offs < DEPTH) & (pos >= 0)
    pos = tl.maximum(pos, 0)   # address safety only; `valid` already encodes pos >= 0, semantics unchanged

(Optionally also `req_state_idx = tl.maximum(req_state_idx, 0)` and mask the `num_computed` load.)

### Validation after the one-line clamp (Ascend 910B3, two nodes)

case  | before  | after
--- | --- | ---
`max_num_seqs=8`, 8 concurrent x128  | crash in 1.5 s  | 8/8 ok
`max_num_seqs=416`, 416 x128  | 4/4 crashed  | 416/416 ok, 3049 tok/s
`max_num_seqs=384`, 384 x128  | crash  | 2621 tok/s (9 rounds, 2605–2633)
c96 / c192 (`5 min warm + 10 min`)  | —  | 1539 / 2098 tok/s
c384 60 min platform  | —  | 2677.3 tok/s (vs 2558.2 before, +4.66%)
GSM8K 50  | —  | 49/50 and 50/50
8 h / 9 rounds soak (c96/c192/c384 + SLO + 8K/32K bursts)  | —  | 0 new devmm, health 200 throughout
8.5 h / 31 rounds soak (each round fills the batch with 416)  | —  | 0 crashes, 0 devmm

### Notes

  * This affects MRV2 only; MRV1 (the default runner) does not use this kernel.
  * Patch used for validation (one line + comment):
`pos = tl.maximum(pos, 0)` right after `valid` is computed.
  * We are happy to open a PR if the direction is acceptable.
